claims.text: Replacing a conventional EAM reference with an on-the-fly trained machine-learning interatomic potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in high-entropy alloys near melting.
CrMnFeNi compositions can constitute multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
CoCrFeNi is an example of an equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloy relevant to the proposed method.
The proposed alloys are to be studied in both solid and liquid states near their melting points.
TOR-TILD uses a static conventional EAM reference potential for thermodynamic integration.
The intervention substitutes that EAM reference with an on-the-fly MLP trained on ab initio liquid configurations.
The intervention is applicable over approximately 0.85–1.0 Tm.
Near melting, the liquid state exhibits a diversity of atomic configurations that is relevant to reference-potential construction.
An MLP trained on liquid configurations captures detailed liquid short-range order.
The MLP captures many-body atomic interactions in the liquid more effectively than the EAM reference.
Training on dynamically sampled ab initio liquid configurations makes the reference energy landscape more representative of the ab initio liquid.
A more representative reference energy landscape improves phase-space overlap between the reference and target systems.
Improved phase-space overlap produces a smoother thermodynamic-integration path and reduces path mismatch relative to an EAM reference.
The intervention will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD's traditional EAM references.
The intervention will yield more precise free-energy calculations for both solid and liquid states.
Conventional EAM references inadequately represent the full diversity of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid state.
Applicability to temperatures outside the near-melting range or to alloys with substantially different bonding remains untested.
Failure to achieve at least a 30% path-mismatch reduction, or failure to improve benchmark free energies significantly, would falsify the hypothesis.
